svg.title: DDR init and training: what is open, what is a blob
svg.desc: Step-by-step DDR initialisation and training on the Avaota-A1 (Allwinner T527, vendor libdram path and mainline U-Boot path) and on the FRDM-IMX93 (NXP i.MX93 with a Synopsys PHY), colour-coded by open source, closed blob on the CPU, closed blob in the PHY microcontroller, PHY hardware engine, ROM, and tool-generated data.
svg.text: DDR init and training: what is open, what is a blob
Avaota-A1 (Allwinner T527) vs FRDM-IMX93 (NXP i.MX93) · from libdram.a symbols (SyterKit), U-Boot dram_sun55i_a523.c, U-Boot drivers/ddr/imx and the FRDM-IMX93 timing file · 2026-10-28

svg.text: A55 + a microcontroller inside the PHY
Boot ROM loads boot0 / SyterKit into SRAM
or FEL over USB (xfel), always available
Boot ROM loads U-Boot SPL into SRAM
or FEL over USB (xfel), always available
Boot ROM + ELE firmware load SPL into OCRAM
signed ELE container · or SDP over USB (uuu)

svg.text: trained CSRs kept for low-power retention
All of it is CPU code.
JTAG + Ghidra can follow every step;
only the PHY engines are black boxes.
All of it is open C.
The gap: what the PHY registers mean.
Training itself is a black box in the PHY:
you set its inputs and read its outputs.
Open source code: read it, change it
Closed blob on the main CPU: step it, reverse it
Closed blob inside the PHY's microcontroller: no stepping
PHY hardware engine: undocumented state machine
Data made by a vendor tool: open file, opaque values
FRDM-IMX95 Pro: same model as the i.MX93, but DDR init runs in the OEI on the Cortex-M33 (imx-oei, BSD-3) and loads Synopsys LPDDR5 training firmware (blob).
The yellow band steps through the rows in order (browsers only). Function names are real symbols; T527 PHY register meanings come from reverse engineering.
